clauses.reason: The only operative command of EO 7995 is its operative paragraph, which exempts William S. Garland from compulsory retirement for age; the held text reads "for a period of one year ending January 31, 1940". The recital states the President's judgment that the public interest requires that William S. Garland, who the recital says will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service during the month of January 1939, be exempted for a period of one year; it commands nothing else. The command is a one-person permission for a stated period, so it ended by its own terms on January 31, 1940; that date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day) under research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md, and the exclusive reading, under which it ends as that day begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see. Later events recorded for this clause: Executive Order No. 8326 of January 22, 1940 grants a further exemption for a period of six months ending July 31, 1940 and recites this order as the exemption already granted; it neither revokes nor alters the period stated in this order, and it is recorded as a later event, not as an end of this clause. A search of the held order texts for this order's number (jobs/claim-kit cruden search) finds it cited only in Executive Order No. 8326 (APP transcription and Photius printing of each), and the later order's own text grants a further period and leaves this order's stated period unchanged, so the stated date remains the first end under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on "further exempt" orders.

research_rationale:
EO 7995 (October 28, 1938, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt) is a one-person order exempting William S. Garland from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year, issued under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a). This is the stale working-text recheck. The earlier claim quoted an American Presidency Project transcription; the working text is now the machine reading of the Government Printing Office printing held in jobs/mabillon-held-printings (grade machine_read_government_printed_copy, acceptable_as_original false; Executive_Orders_7262-8027.djvu; scanned pages 532-533; closing number tag 7995), and the Photius GPO printing of the same order (HathiTrust hvd.hl272j, jobs/photius-gpo-volumes/output/texts/EO_7995.txt) is also held. Standing note: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved. I read the working text in full and compared it word by word with the Photius printing and with the APP transcription: the number, date, title, signatory, authority citation, name of the person and the stated end date agree, and the only differences are OCR noise in the printings (garbled masthead and imprint lines, split or misread letters) that changes no number, date, signatory, name or period. The dateline in the working text reads "October 28, 1988" where the register, the printing and the APP transcription give October 28, 1938 (the year digits are misread; month and day agree). The APP page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl names this order, its date agrees and its text_sha256 equals the held APP file. No page-render row exists for this order in PAGE_CHECKS.csv; the printing text itself carries the closing tag [No. 7995] and the dateline October 28, 1938. The order is one recital paragraph and one operative paragraph (the text contains one "I hereby"), so the clause inventory is one whole-order clause. The operative words "for a period of one year ending January 31, 1940" fix the end of the exemption on January 31, 1940; that is the first end, recorded inclusive, with the exclusive reading disclosed. The packet's later-events and name searches each report 1 hit, and a search of the held order texts for this order's number finds it cited only in EO 8326; I read the held APP text of the later order and compared it with its Photius printing (only OCR differences), and I record it as a later event.

savings.reason: Service performed by William S. Garland while the exemption was in force (through January 31, 1940) is an accrued effect that continues independently of the order; the order states no savings or transition clause.
